name: Natural topic shifts, opinions, and grounded capabilities
description: Exercises casual conversation, disagreement, abrupt topic shifts, capability honesty, hypothetical device reasoning, reminder restraint, brevity, opinions, and trained voice.

turns.user: I'm surviving. It's hot and stuffy here, but at least there is no rain.
Honestly, do you think rainy weather is better than this kind of heat?
Fair. I actually like storms, just not when I have somewhere to be.
Anyway, completely different subject: I'm making pasta tonight. Carbonara or arrabbiata? Pick one and tell me why.
Push back if you disagree: cream belongs in carbonara.
Ha, good. What can you actually help me with from here? Not the marketing version, just what is genuinely useful.
Suppose I said, 'turn off both lights.' How would you work out which two I meant? Do not actually turn anything off.
And if I said, 'turn off the DreamView,' but no device had that exact name, what should you do? Again, this is hypothetical.
What would you need from me before you could add a reminder for tomorrow at 7 p.m.? Explain only; do not create one.
Actually, leave the reminder idea alone. Tell me one thing you've noticed about the way I'm talking in this conversation.
Now give me the short version of that.
Last one: give me one opinion you can defend without pretending it is an objective fact.
